subject: PO vs Card - procurement path and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Johnson <emma@finopsco.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PO vs Card - procurement path and next steps

Hi Emma — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary from today's call:
- FinOpsCo prefers purchase order (PO) for annual/enterprise contracts; corporate card OK for ad-hoc purchases under $10k.
- Procurement requires vendor onboarding packet (W-9 + vendor form) and a security questionnaire before vendor activation.
- Primary commercial path: PO (preferred) but they asked about listing on AWS Marketplace for faster procurement.

Attachments I’m including: vendor-onboarding-form.pdf, W-9 (completed), and a short SOW template you can use to attach to the PO.

Next proposed steps:
1) I’ll share our standard SOW and Redwood procurement guide (attached) so you can route to finance.
2) Lauren (cc'd) is our billing lead — she can provide invoicing details and expedite any vendor questions.
3) If you confirm PO route, can you share your internal PO template or confirm fields you need (billing address, remit-to, tax ID, contact for AP)?
4) I’ll check and confirm our AWS Marketplace status and timeline (if you want that path).

If it helps, we can schedule a short procurement kickoff next week (20-30min) to get vendor onboarding rolling.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

Attachments: vendor-onboarding-form.pdf, W-9_FinOpsCo.pdf, SOW-template.docx

From: Emma Johnson <emma@finopsco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinOpsCo Procurement <procurement@finopsco.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: PO vs Card - procurement path and next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- For anything over $10k we require a PO and vendor setup in our system. Smaller purchases can be done on corporate card.
- Our vendor onboarding always needs an official W-9, completed vendor questionnaire (we'll send the PDF as an attachment in the procurement thread) and a signed MSA (or a DocuSign link).
- Regarding marketplace: we prefer Marketplace listings when available because it speeds approvals, but it's not a blocker.

Could you send our team a short invoice or quote we can attach to the PO (line items and total, and Net30 terms if possible)? Also please confirm whether Redwood can accept Net30 invoices and whether you have an AWS Marketplace listing today or will require 3-4 weeks to onboard.

Thanks — Emma
Emma Johnson
Head of Procurement, FinOpsCo
emma@finopsco.com

(Forwarding the vendor questionnaire to procurement now)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Johnson <emma@finopsco.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO vs Card - procurement path and next steps

Hi Emma — great, thanks for the details. Quick answers: 

- Payment methods: We support both PO/invoice (Net30 by default; Net45/Net60 available for enterprise deals upon request) and corporate card for smaller purchases. For annual contracts most customers go PO/invoice.
- Marketplace: Redwood is available on AWS Marketplace (some SKUs live now); listing additional SKUs or private offers can take 3-6 weeks depending on procurement paperwork. I'll loop in our channel partner lead if you want to pursue that route.
- Invoice/quote: attaching a short invoice template and SOW template you can attach to the PO. If you send over your PO template we'll confirm the exact fields.

Attachments: SOW-template.docx, Redwood-SaaS-Procurement-Guide.pdf

Proposed next steps:
1) If PO: you provide PO template or confirm required fields; Lauren will provide remit-to/billing details.
2) We’ll return completed W-9 and vendor packet (attached) and sign MSA via DocuSign if you prefer.
3) Schedule 20-min procurement kickoff next Tue/Wed to walk through the onboarding form.

Lauren and Rachel — adding you for billing and contract ops.

Best,
Marissa
